function: Unsupervised blind symbol detection (without CSI) for RIS-assisted received spatial modulation, using a K-means-type clustering detector with analytically initialized centroids (p. 1, 4).
system: Passive reflecting RIS with N=64 elements as part of the transmitter, receiver with Nr=4 antennas, flat Rayleigh fading, QPSK and 8QAM; frequency band not stated (p. 1, 5).
method: Unsupervised K-means clustering with centroids initialized from the derived Gaussian distribution of the equivalent channel diagonal; online iterations on the received block, no offline training (p. 4).
data_channel: Own simulator: flat Rayleigh fading, g ~ CN(0,1), AWGN; clustering runs directly on L simulated received signals; no dataset, standard channel model or measurement (p. 2, 5).
test_conditions: No training stage; BER versus SNR for QPSK (Nr,N,L)=(4,64,500) and 8QAM (4,64,1000), and for N=32, 64, 128 RIS elements (p. 5).
baselines: Non-learned: optimal ML and greedy detector with perfect CSI; learned: traditional K-means detectors KMC(1), KMC(P) and KMC(ideal) with known channel (p. 4, 5).
metrics: Bit error rate versus SNR; computational complexity as order and operation count (p. 4, 5).
complexity: Order O(Nr M T2 L); Table I values 8.00x10^3 (M=4, L=500) and 3.20x10^4 (M=8, L=1000), versus ML 5.44x10^5 and 1.15x10^6 (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "assuming flat Rayleigh fading channels". The simulator is custom (g ~ CN(0, 1)); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "increasing N from 32 to 128 significantly enhances BER performance". This is a sweep over the number of RIS elements of a detector with no training stage; no model is trained on one scenario and tested on another.
q3_support: p. 4: "compare it with several traditional clustering detectors"; p. 5: "the greedy detector (GD) and the optimal ML detector with perfect CSI [6]". KMC(1) and KMC(P) are the conventional K-means detectors of [11], [12] (p. 3); GD and ML are non-learned; all are compared on BER (Fig. 3).
q4_support: p. 5: "Table I illustrates the computational complexity of various detectors". Table I gives O(Nr M T2 L) for the proposed detector and the values 8.00x10^3 and 3.20x10^4 for two configurations.
q5_support: p. 4: "simulation results are presented to investigate the performance of the proposed detector". The data are simulated (Rayleigh model, p. 2); the letter gives no link to code or data and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: Title and DOI checked on p. 1 (clustering-based detector for RIS-assisted spatial modulation, 10.1109/LCOMM.2024.3518234). Included although there is no offline training: the detector is an unsupervised clustering algorithm from machine learning (abstract, p. 1) with analytic initial centroids (p. 4); the reviewer should confirm that it counts as learned, otherwise exclude as no_learning. Area 1: blind symbol detection judged by BER; the RIS phases are set by the transmitter to select the receive antenna (p. 2) and are not learned. q3 is a judgement call: KMC(1) and KMC(P) are the conventional K-means detectors of [11], [12] (p. 3, 4) and differ from the proposed detector only by random instead of analytic initialization, so a reviewer who reads them as an ablation should set q3 to 0. Table I (p. 5) was read from the page image.
